subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation surface is clear, but launching `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` and writing prompt drafts to disk crosses product UX and security-boundary choices that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For UX Choice
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and resolve the inactive external-editor keybinding mismatch.

options.title: Decline External Process Handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or plugin-owned editing instead of launching local editors from the TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has already reviewed this exact issue and is the strongest available routing signal for the TUI command/docs/composer surfaces.
